a1.say: Let's build Sign-Up Form With Validation.

a1.cap: Build a sign-up form with email (required, valid), password (min 8 chars) and confirm-password fields. Show errors only after a field is touched, add a custom "passwords match" validator, and disable submit while invalid.

lines: Build a sign-up form with email (required, valid), password (min 8 chars) and confirm-password fields. Show errors only after a field is touched, add a custom "passwords match" validator, and disable submit while invalid.

a1.cap: Reactive forms model the form in TypeScript, which makes validation logic testable and type-safe. NonNullableFormBuilder gives strongly typed controls whose values are never null.
a1.say: Reactive forms model the form in Type Script, which makes validation logic testable and type-safe. Non Nullable Form Builder gives strongly typed controls whose values are never null.

a1.cap: A custom validator on the group compares password and confirmation, and the template shows messages only for touched controls.
A validator is just a function: return null when valid, or an error object.
Standalone components import what their template needs directly.
The form element binds to the FormGroup defined in the class.
a1.say: The form element binds to the Form Group defined in the class.

a1.cap: Show an error only after the user has left the field: touched plus invalid.
Group-level errors live on the form itself.
The submit button stays disabled while anything is invalid.
inject() fetches dependencies without a constructor; the non-nullable builder keeps values typed as string.
